issues.description: transcriber_error listed twice in the tuple — dead duplicate.
issues.detail: Look at the tuple: `transcriber_error` appears on line 3 and again on line 7. It's a set-membership test, so the duplicate does nothing except advertise that nobody read the patch carefully. Delete one. This is the kind of thing that makes the maintainer wonder what else wasn't read carefully.

issues.description: logger.error dropped from the error path with no replacement.
issues.detail: The old code logged each error type before pushing the frame. The new code only calls push_error. If push_error doesn't log at error level (and a quick read says it doesn't reliably), you've made production debugging harder for every error class. Either keep the logger.error, or prove push_error logs and say so in the commit.

issues.description: Error frame payload lost the message-type prefix that used to distinguish auth/quota from generic errors.
issues.detail: Before: `Auth error: ...`, `Quota exceeded: ...`. After: every one of fourteen distinct conditions becomes `Error: ...`. Downstream consumers and humans reading logs can no longer tell an auth failure from a chunk-size violation without parsing the inner string. Include the message_type in the pushed error.

issues.description: Two unrelated changes in one patch — split it.
issues.detail: Patch claims (1) fix infinite-loop on websocket disconnect by removing the swallow-and-log wrapper, and (2) expand error-type coverage. These are independent. When the loop fix needs to be bisected or backported six months from now, it shouldn't drag fourteen new error strings with it. THREE-PATCHES — or at least two.

issues.description: Loop-fix has no test demonstrating the bug or the fix.
issues.detail: The headline claim is an infinite loop on websocket disconnect blocking the whole process. Prose is not a regression suite. Without a test that hangs on the old code and passes on the new, this fix can silently regress the next time someone re-adds defensive try/except around _process_messages. Add the failing-then-passing test.

`No newline at end of file` on changelog/3233.fixed.md. Trivial fixup, but it's the kind of thing the codebase's existing changelog entries presumably don't do. Match the style of the surrounding files.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The loop fix is the right shape — removing the swallow-and-log wrapper so disconnects propagate to the reconnect loop is a correct, small change. But the patch bundles it with an unrelated error-type expansion, and that expansion is sloppy: `transcriber_error` is listed twice, all logger.error calls were dropped, and every error class now collapses to a generic "Error:" prefix that hides which condition actually fired. No test demonstrates the infinite-loop bug or proves it's fixed. Split into two patches, dedupe the tuple, preserve per-type logging and prefix, and add a regression test.
